A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ISG evaluation framework, ISG-BENCH, and ISG-AGENT. Their main text, tables, figures, algorithm, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-alignment evaluations, model benchmarking, and evaluator and agent ablations in Tables 3–7, with additional analyses and examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds resource-use measurements and image-input ablations in Appendix E, Tables 8–12.

M1.justification: The four-level scene-graph evaluation procedure, Algorithm 1, and ISG-AGENT's planning, tool execution, and refinement pipeline remain unchanged. Agent settings move from Section 4.2 to Section 5.2 without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The 1,150 samples, eight categories, and 21 subtasks remain unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds a missing-image input scenario for generation by Show-o and Claude + SD3, extending tested input conditions within the existing benchmark.

E2.justification: Tables 5–6 retain the same unified models and Claude/Gemini combinations with SD3 and SD2.1. The new analyses reuse existing models. GATE OpenING is added to the benchmark-characteristics comparison in Table 1, not as an experimentally evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces generator evaluations with and without image inputs and resource assessments using token consumption, A800 computing times, and API timing estimates assuming 600 tokens per second. The original validation sample counts, scoring procedures, and generation hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E substantially extends supplementary analysis by directly testing the benchmark's dependence on visual inputs across four evaluation levels for two generation frameworks, and by examining evaluation and generation costs. These analyses are distinct from the retained evaluator-input/few-shot ablations in Table 4 and agent-component ablations in Table 7.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same statement that Pearson-correlation P-values are below 0.005. The additions provide point estimates without introducing repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or new significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 retain their numerical entries, but Tables 8–12 add substantial evidence on costs and visual-input dependence. For example, Claude + SD3's holistic average is 3.519 without images versus 6.254 with images; Show-o's corresponding averages are 2.419 and 2.170. These are newly reported ablation comparisons, not performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The graph and tuple representations and Algorithm 1 are retained. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised; the new timing discussion is empirical and interpretive.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the four-level ISG evaluator, ISG-BENCH, and ISG-AGENT. The abstract retains its 111% and 122% improvement claims, and the conclusions about unified-model weaknesses and compositional approaches remain substantively unchanged despite shortened introductory discussion.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds a justification for prioritizing agent performance over resource efficiency and argues that API-based generation times are comparable to unified-model times. It also attributes Show-o's worse holistic scores with images to limited joint visual processing and generation. Existing limitations and future-work discussion are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents token and cost estimates, A800 hardware for timing measurements, the 600-token-per-second API assumption, and cost reductions through batching and prompt caching. Existing implementation prompts, model hyperparameters, and access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds GATE OpenING to Table 1 and cites Chen et al.'s 'Are we on the right way for evaluating large vision-language models?' in the visual-dependence analysis. It removes Yarom et al.'s text-image alignment evaluation reference while condensing related work. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, affiliations, and publication header; condenses introductory, related-work, and concluding prose; moves Discussions and Future Works from Section 6 to Appendix A; and relocates agent settings to Section 5.2. Most existing prose and appendix content remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–12, expands Table 1, places Tables 5–6 together, and substantially redistributes the main-text displays. The comparative radar plots and generation case study move to the appendix, while the agent diagram becomes Figure 5 and several captions are shortened. Retained figures preserve their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: Appendix E improves empirical support for visual-input dependence and makes resource costs more transparent while preserving the established results. The gains are limited: agent timings are estimates rather than comparable end-to-end measurements, and Table 11 does not explain why Show-o's image-input scores differ from Tables 5–6. These gaps constrain the added evidence but do not outweigh its modest benefits.
